sentences.zh: 但它的用户体验要好得多。

sentences.zh: 你只需要在这些不同的因素之间建立连接。

sentences.en: And then you assign weights to the probabilities of various conditions happening.
sentences.zh: 然后为各种条件发生的概率分配权重。

sentences.en: And you can kind of work out things that, at first, would seem very, very complex to determine.

sentences.en: What are these guys talking about?
sentences.zh: 这俩人在聊什么呢？

sentences.en: So, yeah, well, basically, Bayesian networks is, or they're also called, like, deep belief networks.
sentences.zh: 所以，基本上，贝叶斯网络，或者也被称为深度信念网络。

sentences.en: This idea that, like, if, like, they try to figure out if, like, things are correlated, like, if one thing can influence another or not.
sentences.zh: 这个概念是，他们试图找出事物之间是否相关，即一件事是否会影响另一件事。

sentences.en: So, in other words, like, if you tried to see if there was, like, a Bayesian relationship between, like,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果你想看看两者之间是否存在贝叶斯关系，比如，

sentences.en: when you flipped a coin the first time and when you flipped a coin the second time.
sentences.zh: 第一次抛硬币和第二次抛硬币之间。

sentences.en: Like, a deep belief network would tell you, like, no, you know, you flipping a coin the second time, like, is not influenced by flipping it the first time.
sentences.zh: 深度信念网络会告诉你，不，第二次抛硬币不受第一次抛硬币的影响。

sentences.en: Like, if the first time you flipped it and you got heads the second time, you still have a 50-50 chance, you know?
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你第一次抛硬币是正面，第二次你仍然有50%的概率是正面，懂吗？

sentences.en: But, like, something else, like, weather would have a Bayesian relationship.
sentences.zh: 但如果是其他事物，比如天气，就会有贝叶斯关系。

sentences.en: Like, if it rained yesterday, it's probably more likely to rain today than if it didn't rain yesterday.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果昨天下了雨，那么今天下雨的可能性就比昨天没下雨时要大。

sentences.en: You know what I'm saying?

sentences.zh: 比如，他们画出一些概率，然后问，概率会是多少？

sentences.zh: 哇，你今天真是一针见血啊，先生。

sentences.zh: 我们有个关于这个的新闻故事。

sentences.zh: 我想他目前在 Stack Exchange 工作，大多数听众可能都见过这个网站。

sentences.en: And he had an article where he's writing about, I guess he actually posted a video that somebody else about a presentation and then a link to a website.

sentences.en: But it was more just the notion I wanted to talk about, which was that he points out that we've kind of almost regressed in the advancedness of our IDEs,
sentences.zh: 但我更想聊的是他的观点，他指出我们的集成开发环境（IDE）的先进程度几乎退步了，

sentences.en: so integrated developed environments.
sentences.zh: 也就是集成开发环境。

sentences.en: That he's talking about, if we could do better at trying to show programmers the impact of what they're writing, that they could think through the possibilities much more quickly.
sentences.zh: 他说，如果我们能更好地向程序员展示他们所写代码的影响，他们就能更快地思考各种可能性。

sentences.en: So that's kind of vague and okay, I don't know what you're talking about.

sentences.zh: 但从基本层面来说，如果你用过 Eclipse，大多数人第一次用 Eclipse 时。

sentences.en: Maybe less so now because other things do it as well.
sentences.zh: 现在可能少一点了，因为其他工具也能做到。

sentences.en: But they draw the squiggly line, you know, like the incorrect spelling under any sort of compilation error that you have in the code.

sentences.en: And you can just kind of hover it over and it tells you what the error is, offers suggestions.

sentences.en: And this is like a very quick way to actually help you correct the probleMs.

sentences.en: And it's a delight.
sentences.zh: 这简直是一种享受。

sentences.en: And so that's kind of basic level.

sentences.en: So I'm lazier than that.

sentences.en: That's hilarious.

sentences.en: I didn't know that existed.
sentences.zh: 我以前都不知道有这个功能。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: It also deletes anything that you have that isn't being used.
sentences.zh: 它还会删除你没用到的东西。

sentences.en: Like if you have any imports or includes that aren't being used, it goes ahead and removes them for you.
sentences.zh: 比如你有任何没用到的导入或包含，它会直接帮你移除。

sentences.en: So that's like at a basic level.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是基础层面。

sentences.en: But the things that are referenced in this blog article are also even more advanced, which is like if you had like a pathfinding algorithm or a PID,
sentences.zh: 但那篇博客文章里提到的东西更先进，比如如果你有一个寻路算法或 PID，

sentences.zh: 比例-积分-微分，一种控制方法。

sentences.zh: 如果你想看看它如何受到各种输入条件的影响。

sentences.zh: 你可以做图形化表示，让用户通过滑块来观察调整代码中的各种阈值会发生什么。

sentences.en: Or even better, like, you know, take it up a higher dimension and show them like a plot of, you know, on like X, Y,
sentences.zh: 或者更好的是，提升一个维度，给他们展示一个图表，比如在 X、Y 轴上，

sentences.en: here's what various inputs and settings for two different variables will give you.

sentences.zh: 如果能通过这种方式让我们的开发生活更轻松，那该多酷啊？

sentences.en: Yeah, that's awesome, man.
sentences.zh: 是啊，那太棒了，伙计。

sentences.en: I feel like, you know, like IDEs do a pretty good job about code, like, but like, you know, about analyzing code, fixing code, things like that.

sentences.en: And then you have to keep a list of all the things you did.
sentences.zh: 而且你还得保留一份你所做过所有操作的列表。

sentences.en: That probably isn't the way most undoes are written, right?
sentences.zh: 大多数撤销功能的实现方式可能并不是这样，对吧？

sentences.en: The other way is that anytime you do anything, you keep like a snapshot and then undo is just going back through these snapshots, you know?
sentences.zh: 另一种方式是，无论你做什么，都保留一个快照，然后撤销就是回退到这些快照，你懂吗？

sentences.en: But both of those are hard, you know?
sentences.zh: 但这两种方法都很难，你知道吧？

sentences.en: One means you have to be able to serialize, which means, serialize means turn like a bunch of data that you have in memory
sentences.zh: 前者意味着你必须能够进行序列化，也就是说，序列化是指把你内存里的一堆数据，

sentences.en: or like a bunch of things that you're representing, like turn them into a block of ones and zeros that you can load back later.
sentences.zh: 或者你所代表的一堆事物，转换成一串可以稍后重新加载的 0 和 1 的数据块。

sentences.en: So you either have to like serialize everything so that you can deserialize it when you do the undo and then just keep all of these serialized copies of the world around.
sentences.zh: 所以你要么得把一切都序列化，以便在撤销时进行反序列化，然后保留所有这些序列化的世界副本。

sentences.en: Or you have to, as I said before, create like a reverse function for everything.
sentences.zh: 要么就像我之前说的，为每一件事创建一个反向函数。

sentences.en: And I mean, think how hard that is.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，想想这有多难。

sentences.en: Like let's say you have a function that, you know, deletes a line of code.
sentences.zh: 比如，假设你有一个删除一行代码的函数。

sentences.en: Well, the reverse function has to, like you have to have the line of code somewhere so that it can know what you deleted.
sentences.zh: 那么，反向函数必须……你得在某个地方存着那行代码，这样它才知道你删除了什么。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: That kind of, just adding an undo is pretty hard.
sentences.zh: 那种……仅仅是添加一个撤销功能就相当困难。

sentences.en: And so something like this is really hard, but it'd be totally awesome if it was, if we had it.
sentences.zh: 所以像这样的东西真的很难，但如果我们能拥有它，那绝对太棒了。

sentences.en: Oh yeah, I'm totally not saying it's easy.
sentences.zh: 噢，是的，我完全没说这很容易。

sentences.en: It's very hard, yeah.
sentences.zh: 这非常难，确实。

sentences.en: Yeah, yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊，是啊。

sentences.en: But it'd be totally sweet if we had something like that.
sentences.zh: 但如果我们能有那样的功能，那真是太好了。

sentences.en: Like imagine, like.
sentences.zh: 想象一下，就像……

sentences.en: It's one of those things that's interesting to think about.
sentences.zh: 这是那种值得思考的事情之一。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Like you have some kind of game and you're like, oh, what happens if I like change like the AI behavior?
sentences.zh: 比如你玩某种游戏，然后你会想，如果我改变了 AI 的行为会怎样？

sentences.en: If I make the AI more aggressive and like while you're playing, it's like getting more aggressive.
sentences.zh: 如果我让 AI 变得更具攻击性，而且在你玩的时候，它变得越来越激进。

sentences.en: Or what if I change gravity or, you know, it just does all these crazy things.
sentences.zh: 或者如果我改变重力，或者，你知道，它只是做了所有这些疯狂的事情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And I think there are some things that get closer to that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有些东西正越来越接近这一点。

sentences.zh: 比如我不知道你有没有看过 Unity 游戏引擎的演示视频，

sentences.en: but they have some stuff that's kind of like that where it allows you to kind of just jump in the game very quickly
sentences.zh: 但他们有一些类似的东西，允许你非常快速地进入游戏，

sentences.en: and see the effects of the changes you've made and then kind of jump back out.
sentences.zh: 查看你所做更改的效果，然后跳出来。

sentences.en: So there's a lot of news coming out about the next generation of game consoles.
sentences.zh: 所以关于下一代游戏主机有很多新闻传出。

sentences.en: The Wii U, I think, is supposed to be out this year or very soon.
sentences.zh: Wii U 我想应该是在今年或者很快就会发布。

sentences.en: And the next generation Xbox and PlayStation are supposed to be out.
sentences.zh: 还有下一代 Xbox 和 PlayStation 也应该要出了。

sentences.en: And I don't think that Wii U has had anything about this,
sentences.zh: 我不认为 Wii U 有过这方面的消息，

sentences.en: but the Xbox and PlayStation have both had these rumors come out that they're going to block the ability to have used games.
sentences.zh: 但 Xbox 和 PlayStation 都有传言说它们将禁止二手游戏。

sentences.en: So either the distribution will be all online, so think like Steam,
sentences.zh: 所以要么发行将全部在线上进行，想想 Steam，

sentences.en: or that you'll have these one-use codes, which are becoming more and more common in games for at least some portion of the features,
sentences.zh: 要么你会有这种一次性代码，这在游戏中至少对于部分功能来说越来越普遍了，

sentences.zh: 你必须输入序列号或某种激活码才能玩游戏。

sentences.en: And now it's mostly used to play it online or to unlock some special in-game thing.
sentences.zh: 现在它主要用于在线游戏或解锁游戏内的某些特殊内容。

sentences.en: But in the future, you could actually just block the game if you don't have this code.
sentences.zh: 但在未来，如果你没有这个代码，你实际上可能根本无法运行游戏。

sentences.en: And that will not allow people to sell the games when they're done playing them.
sentences.zh: 那将不允许人们在玩完游戏后卖掉它们。

sentences.en: So the way I see it is, I have an Xbox 360, but I don't think, oh, for my birthday I got a game that was new.
sentences.zh: 所以我看来是这样的，我有一台 Xbox 360，但我认为……噢，我生日时收到过一个新游戏。

sentences.en: But aside from that one game, I play only games that are like two years old.
sentences.zh: 但除了那个游戏，我只玩那些大概两年前的游戏。

sentences.en: And I just find, like, I go and look at the magazines online or whatever and find, like, what were the best games of two years ago?
sentences.zh: 我只是发现，我去网上看看杂志之类的，找出两年前最好的游戏是什么？

sentences.en: And then I buy them really cheap used.
sentences.zh: 然后我以很便宜的价格买下二手货。

sentences.en: And I have no desire to play the latest and greatest games.
sentences.zh: 我完全没有兴趣去玩最新最棒的游戏。

sentences.en: I love playing really awesome old games.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢玩那些非常棒的老游戏。

sentences.zh: 而且我能以 5 美元左右的价格买到它们。

sentences.en: And I much prefer doing that.
sentences.zh: 我更喜欢那样做。

sentences.en: And this way won't allow me to do that.
sentences.zh: 而这种方式将不允许我这样做。

sentences.en: But then if you look at something like Steam, I do buy games on Steam, games that are, again, you know, like nine months, a year old.
sentences.zh: 但如果你看看像 Steam 这样的平台，我确实会在 Steam 上买游戏，那些同样是，你知道，九个月、一年前的游戏。

sentences.en: And I can buy them for very, very cheap.
sentences.zh: 我可以以非常非常便宜的价格买到它们。

sentences.en: So what you're saying is, like, if they keep reducing the price over time as the game gets older, then for you as a consumer, it's effectively the same.
sentences.zh: 所以你的意思是，如果他们随着游戏变老不断降低价格，那么对你作为消费者来说，效果是一样的。

sentences.en: But the difference is, instead of GameStop, like, getting this, like, essentially, like, arbitrage, you know, you're buying it straight from the publisher again.
sentences.zh: 但区别在于，不是让 GameStop 获得这种……本质上是套利，你知道，你是直接从发行商那里再次购买。

sentences.en: And the person who would have sold the game new can't.
sentences.zh: 而那个本可以卖出新游戏的人却不能卖了。

sentences.en: So the, yeah, so I don't know exactly what I'm saying.
sentences.zh: 所以……是啊，我不知道我到底在说什么。

sentences.en: But I do think there is an interest here, like, to see what will happen.
sentences.zh: 但我确实认为这里很有趣，看看会发生什么。

sentences.en: And, like, one part of me says, like, oh, it's in their, you know, ability to ban used game sales if they want.
sentences.zh: 一方面我觉得，噢，如果他们想禁止二手游戏销售，那是他们的权利。

sentences.en: But then the other part of me says it's my freedom.
sentences.zh: 但另一方面我觉得这是我的自由。

sentences.en: Like, I should be allowed to sell my game.
sentences.zh: 比如，我应该被允许卖掉我的游戏。

sentences.en: Like, I own the game, and I don't really like the idea of we're going to this subscription or license-based model.
sentences.zh: 比如，我拥有这个游戏，我真的不喜欢我们正在转向这种订阅或基于许可的模式。

sentences.en: Like, you bought this software CD, but you didn't really, you don't own the software.
sentences.zh: 比如，你买了这张软件光盘，但你并没有真正拥有这个软件。

sentences.en: You own permission to rent it for an, you know, unlimited time, but only for you.
sentences.zh: 你拥有的是在无限时间内租用它的许可，但仅限于你个人。

sentences.en: And I don't really like that.
sentences.zh: 我真的不喜欢那样。

sentences.en: Really, yeah.
sentences.zh: 真的，是啊。

sentences.en: You know, a lot of people come up with this argument, like, with music and movies and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，很多人都提出过这个论点，比如针对音乐、电影之类的东西。

sentences.en: Personally, it's never really bothered me.
sentences.zh: 就我个人而言，这从未真正困扰过我。

sentences.en: It only bothers me when Steam goes down, and then, you know, and it's one of these things, it's so funny, right?
sentences.zh: 只有当 Steam 宕机时才会困扰我，然后，你知道，这是那种很搞笑的事情，对吧？

sentences.en: Like, I could go weeks without playing a video game, but then, like, Steam goes down, and it's just, like, instantly, it's like, oh, I really want to play, and I can't.
sentences.zh: 比如，我可以几周不玩电子游戏，但一旦 Steam 宕机，就立刻会觉得，噢，我真的很想玩，但我玩不了。

sentences.en: You know what I mean?
sentences.zh: 你明白我的意思吗？

sentences.en: Like, it's, I don't know, it's like the forbidden fruit, I guess, or something.
sentences.zh: 就像……我不知道，就像禁果，我想，或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: There's some, like, psychological thing going on there.
sentences.zh: 那里发生了一些心理层面的东西。

sentences.en: But, yeah, it's really frustrating when you can't play, because it's down.
sentences.zh: 但是，是的，当因为宕机而无法玩游戏时，真的很令人沮丧。

sentences.en: That's one aspect of it.
sentences.zh: 这是其中的一个方面。

sentences.en: That's kind of annoying, because you could be extended periods of time where you're not, and that would be bad.
sentences.zh: 这有点烦人，因为你可能会有很长一段时间无法玩，那会很糟糕。

sentences.en: But the other thing is, like, I run into occasionally where, like, I have a computer, and then I have my laptop, and then my wife has a computer.
sentences.zh: 但另一件事是，我偶尔会遇到这种情况，比如我有一台电脑，然后我有我的笔记本，我妻子也有一台电脑。

sentences.en: And I feel like, you know, I want my family, like, I don't want to give it to other people, but I want my family to be able to share one version of this.
sentences.zh: 我觉得，你知道，我希望我的家人……我不想把它给别人，但我希望我的家人能够共享这一个版本。

sentences.en: And I don't like the idea that I have to keep buying it over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢我必须一遍又一遍地购买它的想法。

sentences.en: Oh, that's true.
sentences.zh: 噢，那是真的。

sentences.en: But it amounts to, like, one share of juice, because it turns out, like, we're only ever using one at a time.

sentences.zh: 比如，我们中只会有一个人同时使用它。

sentences.en: But we want to be able to have it on different computers at the same time.
sentences.zh: 但我们希望能够同时在不同的电脑上拥有它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.zh: 所以，Steam 某种程度上允许那样，但其他东西就不行了。

sentences.en: It's pretty BS that, like, you can't have two instances of Steam running at the same time.

sentences.zh: 所以，换句话说，我不能在同一个 Steam 账户上玩一个游戏，而我妻子同时玩另一个游戏。

sentences.zh: 比如，不能玩同一个 Steam 游戏，我个人认为这不太公平，但我理解这可能会被滥用，你知道吗？

sentences.en: But if you have three games, you should be able to play all three of them at the same time.

sentences.zh: 怎么说呢，这很难，我没有任何音频背景，所以我不知道该怎么解释，只能说，你知道，这里有一堆按钮，

sentences.en: but not so much that it's overwhelming.
sentences.zh: 但又不会多到让人不知所措。

sentences.en: And the buttons are pretty intuitive, like, like, angry or something like that, you know.
sentences.zh: 而且这些按钮非常直观，比如，比如，愤怒之类的，你知道的。

sentences.en: And you just sort of, like, weld all these adjectives and nouns together and then click random a bunch of times until you get the kind of sound you want.
sentences.zh: 你只需要把这些形容词和名词焊接在一起，然后随机点击几次，直到得到你想要的音效。

sentences.en: And, yeah, definitely if I ever need to make sounds for anything, I'll definitely be using it again.
sentences.zh: 而且，没错，如果我以后需要为任何东西制作音效，我肯定会再次使用它。

sentences.zh: 那么，你知道，如果你要开发一款游戏，你会使用什么编程语言？

sentences.en: Well, if I was making a game, I'd probably, I'd want something that had, like, a lot of performance, so I'd definitely be writing that in C++.
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果我要开发游戏，我可能会想要一种性能很强的语言，所以我肯定会用 C++ 来写。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.zh: 好吧，这可能有点不公平，但这正好引出了我们本期的编程语言主题。

sentences.en: It's a shame we haven't talked about C++ and people just can't make games because, you know, we haven't given them any guidance.
sentences.zh: 遗憾的是我们还没聊过 C++，而人们却无法制作游戏，因为，你知道，我们还没给他们任何指导。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think there's other ways to make games, too.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我想还有其他制作游戏的方法。

sentences.en: Yeah, probably.
sentences.zh: 没错，大概吧。

sentences.en: Anyways.
sentences.zh: 总之。

sentences.en: So, the history of C++.
sentences.zh: 那么，C++ 的历史。

sentences.en: Now, C++ is obviously the++ meaning that it wasn't the first, so there was something before it.
sentences.zh: 现在，C++ 显然那个“++”意味着它不是第一个，所以它之前还有别的东西。

sentences.en: And we've talked about that before.
sentences.zh: 我们之前也聊过这个。

sentences.en: That was C.
sentences.zh: 那就是 C 语言。

sentences.en: Totally.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And somebody had the idea to kind of make C better.
sentences.zh: 有人想到了一个让 C 语言变得更好的主意。

sentences.en: And that person was, would you care to pronounce?
sentences.zh: 那个人是，你愿意试着读一下他的名字吗？

sentences.en: I'll do my beSt.
sentences.zh: 我会尽力的。

sentences.en: I think it's Bjarn Straustrup.
sentences.zh: 我想是 Bjarn Straustrup。

sentences.en: I don't know if that's right or not.
sentences.zh: 我不知道读得对不对。

sentences.en: I've actually only read the name, so never actually pronounced it.
sentences.zh: 我其实只读过这个名字，从来没真正读出声来。

sentences.en: Yeah, so he, Mr. Straustrup, we're going to get all sorts of corrections, I'm sure.
sentences.zh: 是啊，所以他，Straustrup 先生，我敢肯定我们会收到各种各样的纠正。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, he had the idea that, you know, he wanted to add classes to C.
sentences.zh: 是啊，他当时的想法是，你知道，他想给 C 语言增加类（classes）。

sentences.en: And so, you know, with anything, as C was coming out, people were hesitant because they wanted to write everything in an assembly.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，和任何事物一样，当 C 语言刚出来时，人们很犹豫，因为他们想用汇编语言编写一切。

sentences.en: And then, as C++ came out, you know, oh, we're going to have these classes thing.
sentences.zh: 然后，当 C++ 出来时，你知道，哦，我们要有这些“类”的东西了。

sentences.en: He wanted to be able to show people, look, it really is just kind of like C, but better.
sentences.zh: 他想向人们展示，看，它其实就像 C 语言，但更好。

sentences.en: And so, the original compiler was actually just to compile C++ to C.
sentences.zh: 所以，最初的编译器其实只是把 C++ 编译成 C 语言。

sentences.en: And then use the existing C compilers to generate machine code.
sentences.zh: 然后再使用现有的 C 编译器来生成机器码。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, if you put yourself in his shoes, like, people had been really working on C compilers for a long time.
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果你设身处地为他着想，人们已经在 C 编译器上投入了很长时间的工作。

sentences.en: You know, and they were highly optimized and things like that.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们经过了高度优化等等。

sentences.en: And, you know, you want to invent your own language.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，你想发明自己的语言。

sentences.en: If you make your own compiler to assembly, it's not going to be anywhere near as good as C, you know, because they've done so many optimizations.
sentences.zh: 如果你自己写一个直接编译成汇编的编译器，它的性能绝对赶不上 C 语言，你知道，因为他们已经做了太多的优化。

sentences.en: So, you know, as a first step, it makes sense.
sentences.zh: 所以，作为第一步，这是有道理的。

sentences.en: So, you wrote the C++ compiler to go to C, and then you can use your highly optimized C compiler.
sentences.zh: 所以，你写了 C++ 编译器来转换成 C，然后你就可以使用你高度优化的 C 编译器了。

sentences.en: It's sort of like what's going on now with LLVM.
sentences.zh: 这有点像现在 LLVM 的做法。

sentences.en: Yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 没错，没错。

sentences.en: And, I mean, people eventually, you know, started to come around and say, wow, this is nice.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，人们最终，你知道，开始接受并说，哇，这真不错。

sentences.en: But there was the original versions, and you'll still hear if you go to somewhere where people have been programming for a long time,
sentences.zh: 但最初的版本确实存在，如果你去那些人们长期从事编程的地方，你仍然会听到，

sentences.en: especially performant programs for a long time.
sentences.zh: 尤其是长期从事高性能程序开发的地方。

sentences.en: A lot of people still have a hesitancy of C++ because they think it's so much more inefficient than C.
sentences.zh: 很多人对 C++ 仍然有顾虑，因为他们认为它比 C 语言效率低得多。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And that just has to do with the idea that, you know, those original versions, when you were translating from the C++ to the C,
sentences.zh: 这仅仅是因为那个想法，你知道，那些最初的版本，当你把 C++ 转换成 C 时，

sentences.en: it generated, you know, kind of more C code than a hand-coded C program.
sentences.zh: 它生成的 C 代码比手写的 C 程序要多。

sentences.en: Just like, you know, a program written in C generates typically more instructions than a hand-coded assembly program.
sentences.zh: 就像，你知道，用 C 语言编写的程序通常比手写的汇编程序生成的指令更多一样。

sentences.en: Yep.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Yeah, totally.
sentences.zh: 是啊，完全同意。

sentences.en: I mean, I think that one of the things, too, is, and, you know, we've touched on this before, but just to recap,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我认为其中一点也是，而且，你知道，我们之前提到过，但简单回顾一下，

sentences.en: it's, in the end, it really comes down to how you use the language.
sentences.zh: 归根结底，这真的取决于你如何使用这门语言。

sentences.en: Like, for C++, for example, you know, as we mentioned, it's C with classes.
sentences.zh: 比如，以 C++ 为例，你知道，正如我们提到的，它是带类的 C 语言。

sentences.en: If you have, you know, let's say you're doing some kind of, like, fluid dynamics, right?
sentences.zh: 如果你有，比如，假设你在做某种流体动力学模拟，对吧？

sentences.en: And so you have a bunch of cells which have, you know, water in them that are moving in a certain direction.
sentences.zh: 所以你有一堆单元格，里面有水，正朝着某个方向移动。

sentences.en: Well, if you make a separate class for every cell and then you try and do some kind of fluid dynamics where you go to all the classes
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你为每个单元格创建一个单独的类，然后尝试进行某种流体动力学计算，遍历所有的类，

sentences.en: and then in each class you do some, like, computation, that's going to be way slower than just having an array of floats, right?
sentences.zh: 然后在每个类中进行一些计算，那会比仅仅使用一个浮点数数组要慢得多，对吧？

sentences.en: Or something like that.
sentences.zh: 或者类似的东西。

sentences.en: So, like, that's an example where, like, you don't really want to make a class for, like, everything.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个例子，你并不真的想为每样东西都创建一个类。

sentences.en: You just want an array of floats and then maybe just one class that does, like, the fluid dynamics for the whole world or whatever, you know?
sentences.zh: 你只需要一个浮点数数组，然后可能只需要一个类来处理整个世界的流体动力学，或者其他什么，你知道吗？

sentences.en: So, you know, in the beginning, with most languages, people, it's a combination of the language isn't optimized,
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，起初，对于大多数语言，人们，这是语言本身没有优化，

sentences.en: but then also people don't really know what to do with the language.
sentences.zh: 但同时人们也不知道该如何使用这门语言。

sentences.en: Yeah, that's a good point.
sentences.zh: 没错，这是一个很好的观点。

sentences.en: Yeah, over time, people start, you know, the language, as it gets more adoption, people start to understand the best ways to use it.
sentences.zh: 是啊，随着时间的推移，人们开始，你知道，这门语言，随着它的普及，人们开始理解使用它的最佳方式。

sentences.en: Now, C++ doesn't have versions like some other languages.
sentences.zh: 现在，C++ 不像其他一些语言那样有版本号。

sentences.en: Like, there's not C++ 1.0, 2.0.
sentences.zh: 比如，没有 C++ 1.0, 2.0 之类的。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: There's nothing like that.
sentences.zh: 没有那种东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, but the...
sentences.zh: 是啊，但是……

sentences.en: Yep, go ahead.
sentences.zh: 没错，请继续。

sentences.en: Oh, there is a new version coming out, and have you studied this at all?
sentences.zh: 哦，确实有一个新版本要出来了，你研究过这个吗？

sentences.en: I did look into it a little, you know, having some background in C++.
sentences.zh: 我确实稍微看了一下，你知道，毕竟我有 C++ 背景。

sentences.en: I was very intrigued, like, oh, they're upgrading, you know, what are they going to add?
sentences.zh: 我非常感兴趣，比如，哦，他们要升级了，你知道，他们要增加什么？

sentences.en: Like, how are they going to bring this into the, you know, kind of 21st century?
sentences.zh: 比如，他们打算如何把它带入 21 世纪？

sentences.en: And so it was originally, you know, going to be called C++, you know, 0x or whatever, you know, implying that it would come out in the single digits of the 2000s.
sentences.zh: 所以它最初，你知道，被称为 C++ 0x 之类的，你知道，暗示它会在 2000 年代的个位数年份发布。

sentences.en: But they kind of missed that deadline in getting agreement on what they were going to put in.
sentences.zh: 但他们错过了那个截止日期，没能就放入什么内容达成一致。

sentences.en: So I think the official name ended up being C++11.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为最终的正式名称是 C++11。

sentences.en: Oh, I didn't know that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不知道这一点。

sentences.en: Coming out in 2011.
sentences.zh: 在 2011 年发布。

sentences.en: I always thought it was C++ TR1 or something.
sentences.zh: 我一直以为是 C++ TR1 之类的。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Well, I think that was one of the early versions of the 0x before it got fully ratified or whatever.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我想那是 0x 的早期版本之一，在它完全批准之前。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: And so C++11, which we haven't talked about all about what C++ has,
sentences.zh: 所以 C++11，我们还没聊过 C++ 到底有什么，

sentences.en: but they just try to make the language a little easier to use while at the same time keeping it being powerful and adding, try to add some stuff for, you know,
sentences.zh: 但他们只是试图让这门语言更容易使用，同时保持它的强大，并尝试增加一些东西，为了，你知道，

sentences.en: the idea of multi-threading and concurrency, which wasn't as big when C++, of course, was in earlier versions, and then just making some things nicer,
sentences.zh: 多线程和并发的概念，这在 C++ 早期版本时当然没那么重要，然后就是让一些事情变得更好，

sentences.en: like kind of inferring what values should be as opposed to having to make them explicit.
sentences.zh: 比如推断数值应该是什么，而不是必须显式地写出来。

sentences.en: Or if you have like a constant function, you can create an array by calling that function and, you know, like adding a number to it.
sentences.zh: 或者如果你有一个常量函数，你可以通过调用该函数来创建一个数组，并且，你知道，比如给它加一个数字。

sentences.en: So like if you have a function that just returns the number five, you can make the size of the static array be, you know, calling this function plus two.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你有一个只返回数字 5 的函数，你可以让静态数组的大小为，你知道，调用这个函数加 2。

sentences.en: And it knows to make it seven, whereas before that would have been illegal because in C++, the static arrays, you know, have to have a constant size definition.
sentences.zh: 它知道要把它设为 7，而在此之前这是非法的，因为在 C++ 中，静态数组必须有常量大小定义。

sentences.en: Gotcha.
sentences.zh: 懂了。

sentences.en: Yeah, one of the big things that's in the new C++ that, you know, it's probably, actually it's probably not that big,
sentences.zh: 是啊，新 C++ 中的一大亮点，你知道，它可能，其实可能没那么大，

sentences.en: but it's really important for me anyways because it's good for people who want to develop quickly is something called a shared pointer.
sentences.zh: 但对我来说真的很重要，因为它对那些想要快速开发的人很有帮助，那就是所谓的共享指针（shared pointer）。

sentences.en: And so what this is, is, as we talked about in the C podcast, you know, C++ and C, most of the time you're dealing with pointers that you allocate.
sentences.zh: 所以这是什么呢，正如我们在 C 语言播客中讨论的那样，你知道，C++ 和 C，大多数时候你处理的是你分配的指针。

sentences.en: So you say, you know, hey, computer, give me a chunk of memory so that I can do something with it.
sentences.zh: 所以你说，你知道，嘿，电脑，给我一块内存，这样我就可以用它做点什么。

sentences.en: And usually, you know, in C++, in C, you'll say malloc.
sentences.zh: 通常，你知道，在 C++ 和 C 中，你会说 malloc。

sentences.en: In C++, you say new.
sentences.zh: 在 C++ 中，你说 new。

sentences.en: But they do like close to the same thing.
sentences.zh: 但它们做的事情几乎一样。

sentences.en: And then later on, when you're done with that memory, in C, you would say free, and then the chunk of memory.
sentences.zh: 然后稍后，当你用完那块内存时，在 C 中，你会说 free，然后是那块内存。

sentences.en: In C++, you say delete.
sentences.zh: 在 C++ 中，你说 delete。

sentences.en: But it's the same kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 但这是同样的事情。

sentences.en: Once you're done with the memory, you have to delete it.
sentences.zh: 一旦你用完了内存，你就必须删除它。

sentences.en: Otherwise, you're in control of memory management.
sentences.zh: 否则，你就得负责内存管理。

sentences.en: Right, right.
sentences.zh: 对，对。

sentences.en: And if you don't delete the memory, then eventually you will run out of memory because you'll just keep creating, asking the computer for memory and not returning it back.
sentences.zh: 如果你不删除内存，那么最终你会耗尽内存，因为你会一直创建，一直向电脑索要内存却不归还。

sentences.en: Right, you'll leak memory.
sentences.zh: 对，你会内存泄漏。

sentences.en: So what shared pointer does is you wrap your new inside the phrase shared pointer and it knows when to delete it.
sentences.zh: 所以共享指针的作用是，你把你的 new 包装在共享指针里，它就知道什么时候该删除它。

sentences.en: So basically, it does what's called reference counting.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，它做了所谓的引用计数。

sentences.en: So if you say, like, shared pointer x equals new int.
sentences.zh: 所以如果你说，比如，shared pointer x equals new int。

sentences.en: Well, now, like, x points to a reference.
sentences.zh: 好吧，现在，x 指向一个引用。

sentences.en: x contains a reference saying, hey, right now x is using int.
sentences.zh: x 包含一个引用，说，嘿，现在 x 正在使用这个 int。

sentences.en: So, you know, we got to keep it around.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，我们得保留它。

sentences.en: Then later on, if you say y equals x, now there's two references.
sentences.zh: 然后稍后，如果你说 y equals x，现在有两个引用了。

sentences.en: So, like, behind the scenes, it's saying, hey, you know, two people, y and x, are both using this integer, so we can't free it.
sentences.zh: 所以，在后台，它在说，嘿，你知道，两个人，y 和 x，都在使用这个整数，所以我们不能释放它。

sentences.en: And then eventually your program keeps running, keeps running.
sentences.zh: 然后你的程序继续运行，继续运行。

sentences.en: And then just as part of the program, y and x, let's say, fall out of scope.
sentences.zh: 然后作为程序的一部分，y 和 x，假设，超出了作用域。

sentences.en: Like, maybe they're part of another shared pointer.
sentences.zh: 比如，也许它们是另一个共享指针的一部分。

sentences.en: Like, they're in a class that is itself contained in a shared pointer or your program ends or whatever.
sentences.zh: 比如，它们在一个本身包含在共享指针里的类中，或者你的程序结束了等等。

sentences.en: It says, hey, there's no more references to this int, so now I can free this int.
sentences.zh: 它说，嘿，没有更多对这个 int 的引用了，所以现在我可以释放这个 int 了。

sentences.en: So it does all the freeing for you.
sentences.zh: 所以它为你完成了所有的释放工作。

sentences.en: That's one really nice thing that was added in the new C++.
sentences.zh: 这是新 C++ 中增加的一个非常好的功能。

sentences.en: So does that mean they've added garbage collection to C++?
sentences.zh: 那这是否意味着他们给 C++ 增加了垃圾回收机制？

sentences.en: Boy, that's a hard question to answer.
sentences.zh: 天哪，这是一个很难回答的问题。

sentences.en: I guess technically, so for people, I don't know if we've explained garbage collection.
sentences.zh: 我想从技术上讲，对于人们，我不知道我们是否解释过垃圾回收。

sentences.en: I think we did a little when we talked about Java, but I'm not sure.
sentences.zh: 我想我们在聊 Java 时稍微提过，但不确定。

sentences.en: Oh, okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，好的。

sentences.en: Well, we'll explain it just really quick.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们简单解释一下。

sentences.en: Garbage collection is the idea that, you know, over time, there are, so some languages like Java, you don't free things.
sentences.zh: 垃圾回收的概念是，你知道，随着时间的推移，有些语言像 Java，你不需要手动释放内存。

sentences.en: And, but because of, there's like, actually, so no, to answer the question now, now that I thought about it, no, it doesn't implement garbage collection.
sentences.zh: 但是因为，实际上，所以不，回答这个问题，现在我想到了，不，它没有实现垃圾回收。

sentences.en: And so what that means is, let's say you have shared pointer x that points to some class.
sentences.zh: 这意味着，假设你有一个指向某个类的共享指针 x。

sentences.en: And then that class has a shared pointer y that points to x.
sentences.zh: 然后那个类有一个指向 x 的共享指针 y。

sentences.en: So you have a loop, right?
sentences.zh: 所以你有一个循环，对吧？

sentences.en: So x refers to something that has y, and y refers back to something that has x.

sentences.zh: 即使你并不一定知道哪个是正方形，哪个是圆形，你知道它们都有“获取面积”函数，因为它们扩展了或者

sentences.en: places in your program.

sentences.en: So you'll have, like, a float list, you'll have an int list, you'll have a, you know, a shape liSt.

sentences.en: And that is powerful.

sentences.en: The reason that it does that allows you to do, which we won't get into, because I don't even know if you could describe it in a podcast, it'd be kind of hard verbally,
sentences.zh: 它之所以能做到这一点，是因为它允许你做一些事情，我们就不深入探讨了，因为我甚至不知道你是否能在播客里描述它，口头表达会很难，

sentences.zh: 但这就是模板元编程。

sentences.en: Which are programs that you write that get run at compile time, not at runtime.
sentences.zh: 也就是你编写的在编译时运行，而不是在运行时运行的程序。

sentences.zh: 所以有些事情你需要做。

sentences.zh: 假设你的程序里有 3 加 4。

sentences.zh: 嗯，你知道，计算机，编译器不知道那是 7。

sentences.en: The compiler, like, you have to actually run the program, and then your computer, once running the program, will do the 3 plus 4 and then return 7.
sentences.zh: 编译器，就像，你必须实际运行程序，然后你的计算机在运行程序时，会做 3 加 4 然后返回 7。

sentences.en: But there are some things, like some computations, that need to be known at what's called at compile time.
sentences.zh: 但有些事情，比如一些计算，需要在所谓的编译时就知道。

sentences.en: So, like, while the compiler is compiling, it needs to know that this 3 plus 4 is 7, or this X plus Y is whatever it is.
sentences.zh: 所以，比如，当编译器在编译时，它需要知道这个 3 加 4 是 7，或者这个 X 加 Y 是多少。

sentences.en: And so, to actually do this plus at compile time, you can actually do things like this using what's called, as Patrick mentioned, template metaprogramming.

sentences.en: But it's pretty, it's very rare that you have to do something like that, but it does come up.

sentences.zh: C++ 增加的另一个特性是运算符重载。

sentences.en: So, once you define a class, it would be really nice if you could do something, you know, like, I want to add two of my classes together.

sentences.zh: 并以一种我定义的类所特有的方式将它们相加。

sentences.en: And so, I want to redefine how the plus is, what happens when I say, you know, my shape
sentences.zh: 因此，我想重新定义加号的作用，或者当我输入“我的形状”时会发生什么，

sentences.en: and then the plus sign, or, you know, my probability, the plus sign, and then, you know, another instance of my probability.
sentences.zh: 然后是加号，或者，你知道，我的概率，加号，然后是，你知道，我的概率的另一个实例。

sentences.zh: 但确实，正如 Patrick 所提到的，C++ 显然有运算符重载，而且它非常棒。

sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.zh: 那可能会引发矛盾。

sentences.en: Awesome.

sentences.en: So, and to test it became hard to debug, because, you know, it'd literally take a minute,

sentences.zh: 所以，假设我正在开发某个图形引擎，我可以随便拼凑一些 .h 文件，我可以写，好吧，我知道会有一个图形引擎，它会

sentences.en: to, and as long as if my program has permission to write there, I can write whatever I want to that.

sentences.zh: 所以，现在我的 size 变量被设置为 10，然后我写了这个从 1 到 size 的 for 循环，

sentences.en: And C++, it won't give you an error or a crash or anything like that.

sentences.en: know, you're just, you're reading memory that doesn't make sense, but you're not crashing, you're getting data, it's just bogus, and so these are incredibly hard to debug.
